title: A drawing shows what was asked, pose and all: a cat curled up asleep, a cat playing a piano
goal: When a person asks for a thing in a pose or doing something ('a cat curled up sleeping'), or for several things in a relationship ('a cartoon cat playing a piano', 'a dog chasing a ball', 'a fox sleeping under a tree'), Ask draws one picture where they really do that: the cat sits at the piano, its paws on the keys, both at sensible sizes and in one style. Today it drops two stock drawings on top of each other.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-20 15:35 (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-cat-playing-piano.png): asked 'draw a piano with a cartoon cat playing it'. Ask made two add_drawing steps (row 'Drew 2 drawings'): a built-in cat drawing (Twemoji-style, the dog task's built-in set) placed over most of a built-in upright piano, which shows only as a dark edge behind the cat. User: 'It stuffed a cat on top of some keys. horrible. but it makes some logical sense.'

Cause, likely: the planner splits a scene into nouns and calls add_drawing per noun (Sources/PhotonzCore/AskPlanning.swift, instructions around :504 say add_drawing once with its subject); nothing plans the relationship, pose or placement. Waits on the illustration task (in progress), whose passes (composition, shapes, light) are where a scene belongs.

Second report, 2026-10-20 15:37: 'it only seems to know how to draw 1 cat. if i ask it to draw a cat curled up sleeping, same cat.' The built-in set (from ask-draws-a-dog-you-can-tell-is-a-dog, Twemoji) is looked up by the noun and drops every modifier. The fix is the same as for the piano: plan the subject with its pose and relations first, then pick a built-in only if it matches the plan, else draw it.

The user, 2026-10-20: 'the cat task is just an example ... i don't want a hardcoded anything.' Every case named in this task is an example of the bar. Coding a cat, a piano or a pose for them breaks the hard rule in queue/bin/runner-prompt.md.
acceptance: 'draw a piano with a cartoon cat playing it' on a blank picture gives a cat seated or standing at the piano, facing the keys, paws on the keys, the piano in a view where the keys show, the two at believable relative sizes, nothing of one hidden by the other by accident, in one shared style and palette

A pose, action, view, colour or mood in the request changes the drawing: 'a cat curled up sleeping' is a cat curled into a ball with its eyes shut and tail wrapped round, not the standing cat. Nothing is looked up from a stored set (the user's picture: the user's picture: queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-cat-sleeping-same-cat.png). Eval cases (climb set): a rabbit curled up asleep, a cat jumping, a black cat seen from behind, a happy dog sitting, an angry bird, each judged on didWhatWasAsked at 7 or more

The relationship is planned before drawing (who, where, doing what, which parts touch, what is in front), and the plan is checked from the read document: the paws' layers touch the keys' layer, the cat overlaps the piano only where the plan says

No stored or coded subject is used for any part of a scene: the scene is planned (who, where, doing what) and drawn by the general route of ask-draws-any-subject-well-with-nothing-stored-o. The cases here are examples of the bar, not things to code

Six scene cases join the eval's climb set (a cat playing a guitar, a dog chasing a ball, a fox sleeping under a tree, a robot watering a plant, a bird on a branch singing, a child flying a kite), each scoring 7 or more on didWhatWasAsked and designed, and the held-out total (Scripts/ask-eval.sh report) rises; the user's picture (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-cat-playing-piano.png) scores 3 or lower on didWhatWasAsked

The row names the scene ('Drew a cat playing a piano'), and the whole scene is one change. Audit under queue/audits/ with before and after contact sheets and scores. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

Before building (adversarial): a first-time user typing 'a cat playing a guitar' expects one picture where the cat holds it; the app can deliver that with the picture model painting the whole scene, but nothing checked the pose or the relationship. The look only asked a blind model to NAME the drawing, so 'black cat seen from behind' passed when seen as 'cat' (reproduced in baseline run 20261022-073410-ask: black cat 45, didWhatWasAsked 4; robot watering a plant had no can; fox's tree cut flat along the picture edge).

Chose to check the plan from the rendered drawing over checking which layers touch in the read document, because painted drawings trace into colour regions ('Dark brown 3'), not parts, so 'the paws' layers touch the keys' layer' has no layers to read; the model that sees answers yes or no per statement instead.

Chose to keep a drawing that reads as the thing but still misses part of its plan after the last try, over undoing it and saying it could not draw, because throwing away a recognisable scene for one missed detail leaves the person with nothing.

Learned on the way: plans padded with unasked statements ('centred', 'the only subject', 'the branch spans the canvas') made the check repaint good drawings three times (run 20261022-075005-ask, up to 203 s); plans now cover only what the request names. A general look line 'a dark subject keeps lighter inner lines' made the picture model paint cats and dogs black, reverted. Saying a view as the eye sees it ('we see the back of its head and both ears; no face shows') got rear views the word 'behind' did not. A model resent a scene's add_drawing with its plan reworded and two whole pictures stacked (dog chasing a ball 52.9); a second drawing landing on the first is now refused. Prompt examples that were the user's own held-out requests (cat curled up asleep, cat playing a piano) were swapped for ones that are no eval case.

Cause found: the kite was painted as a scene, the painting had the string running to the child's hand, and scene tracing (layers.py: GaussianBlur 3 then a mode filter of 7, 14 colours, there so a sky bands smoothly) wiped out the thin pale string; the plan check then said yes to a string that was gone. What is left: keep thin lines through scene tracing without bringing back ragged skies, then re-measure the six scenes and the held-out total.
